records.text: A passed pawn has no enemy pawn ahead on its own or neighboring files. White has one now; the next distinction is whether pieces can stop it.
A passed pawn has no enemy pawn ahead on its own or neighboring files. Black has one now; the next distinction is whether pieces can stop it.
The alternative would have given White a passed pawn. Remember the distinction: passed does not mean beyond capture.
The alternative would have given Black a passed pawn. Remember the distinction: passed does not mean beyond capture.
White is left with an isolated pawn. Its neighboring files contain no friendly pawns, though pieces may still defend it.
Black is left with an isolated pawn. Its neighboring files contain no friendly pawns, though pieces may still defend it.
Another move would have left White a pawn without friendly pawns on adjacent files. That is the isolated-pawn pattern.
Another move would have left Black a pawn without friendly pawns on adjacent files. That is the isolated-pawn pattern.
White's pawns now share a file: doubled pawns. Whether that structure helps or hurts depends on the whole position.
Black's pawns now share a file: doubled pawns. Whether that structure helps or hurts depends on the whole position.
The doubled-pawn pattern must be judged within the whole position. It would arise for White after the better move, with pawns sharing a file.
The doubled-pawn pattern must be judged within the whole position. It would arise for Black after the better move, with pawns sharing a file.
White's rook now occupies an open file. Open, in this case, means free of every pawn, not every piece.
Black's rook now occupies an open file. Open, in this case, means free of every pawn, not every piece.
An open file excludes pawns, not every obstacle. The alternative would have placed White's rook on just such a file.
An open file excludes pawns, not every obstacle. The alternative would have placed Black's rook on just such a file.
White's rook now has a half-open file. White has no pawns there, while Black still does; that is the distinction from an open file.
Black's rook now has a half-open file. Black has no pawns there, while White still does; that is the distinction from an open file.
A half-open file has enemy pawns but no friendly pawns. That is the pattern White's rook would have after the alternative move.
A half-open file has enemy pawns but no friendly pawns. That is the pattern Black's rook would have after the alternative move.
A piece's strength and its support are different things. This move gives White's knight the defender it lacked.
A piece's strength and its support are different things. This move gives Black's knight the defender it lacked.
White's bishop has gained the guard it lacked. A defender is a connection worth tracing on the board.
Black's bishop has gained the guard it lacked. A defender is a connection worth tracing on the board.
An old principle: a lone piece invites trouble. White's rook now has the defender it was missing.
An old principle: a lone piece invites trouble. Black's rook now has the defender it was missing.
The queen needs defenders too. White's queen had none, and this move supplies protection.
The queen needs defenders too. Black's queen had none, and this move supplies protection.
Count support apart from a piece's own strength. The better move would give White's knight the defender it lacked.
Count support apart from a piece's own strength. The better move would give Black's knight the defender it lacked.
A familiar gap would have closed with the better move: White's bishop, unguarded until then, would have gained a defender.
A familiar gap would have closed with the better move: Black's bishop, unguarded until then, would have gained a defender.
The alternative would have given White's rook a defender. Such connections hold a position together.
The alternative would have given Black's rook a defender. Such connections hold a position together.
Old wisdom holds that no piece guards itself. The better move would have given White's queen a defender.
Old wisdom holds that no piece guards itself. The better move would have given Black's queen a defender.
White's knight has lost all its defenders. That is a fact about support, not yet a verdict that the knight is lost.
Black's knight has lost all its defenders. That is a fact about support, not yet a verdict that the knight is lost.
The guarding connection is gone: White's bishop has no defender now. Notice what the move has changed.
The guarding connection is gone: Black's bishop has no defender now. Notice what the move has changed.
White's rook is now undefended; its previous protection has disappeared. Whether a capture works requires another step of calculation.
Black's rook is now undefended; its previous protection has disappeared. Whether a capture works requires another step of calculation.
White's queen has lost its last guard. The queen's strength does not replace a defender.
Black's queen has lost its last guard. The queen's strength does not replace a defender.
Under the alternative, White's knight would have lost its last defender. Undefended and capturable are distinct questions.
Under the alternative, Black's knight would have lost its last defender. Undefended and capturable are distinct questions.
Another move would have removed the remaining protection from White's bishop. Include that in the comparison.
Another move would have removed the remaining protection from Black's bishop. Include that in the comparison.
White's rook would have been left without a defender by the alternative. That alone would not prove a material loss.
Black's rook would have been left without a defender by the alternative. That alone would not prove a material loss.
A different move would have stripped White's queen of its last guard. Even for a queen, support deserves attention.
A different move would have stripped Black's queen of its last guard. Even for a queen, support deserves attention.
Development begins with departure. This knight has left its original square for the first time.
A piece begins development by leaving home. This is the knight's first such move.
A knight leaves its starting square for the first time. Mark its first step in development.
Here the familiar opening task is visible: a knight moves from its original square for the first time.
The bishop sets out along its diagonals for the first time. Every opening asks this of its bishops.
The bishop had not yet left home. Its first departure gives a concrete example of development.
A bishop leaves home for the first time. It will keep to squares of one color for the rest of the game.
An old opening duty fulfilled: this bishop has left its original square for the first time.
Development offers a point of comparison: another move would have brought a knight off its home square for the first time.
The alternative would have started a knight's development. It had not yet left its original square.
A different move would have been the knight's first departure from home. Consider that opening task in the comparison.
Another choice would have developed the knight from its starting square for the first time. Consider where it would stand.
The alternative would have called a bishop out from its home square for the first time. Weigh that in the comparison.
The better move would have settled an old opening matter: this bishop would have left home for the first time.
In the better line, a bishop would have made its first departure. Unmoved pieces are a pattern worth noticing.
A bishop's first journey lay in the better choice. The opening has long turned on such journeys.
A move's cost is measured against the available choice. This leaves less than the stronger move would have.
This falls below what the position offered. Compare the better move before deciding what has been surrendered.
Judge the choice against what else was available. This move leaves a poorer position than the stronger alternative.
The stronger choice preserves more of the position's value. This move gives some of that away.
Begin with the immediate reply: the other side can capture at once.
There is no intervening move needed for the capture. The other side has it available now.
An immediate capture belongs in the calculation here. Establish what can be taken before weighing the exchange.
First consider the available capture in reply. Its existence and its value are different questions.
An error matters when it is used. You have made use of the opponent's previous mistake.
The opportunity arose on the preceding move, and you answered it correctly. A fine practical lesson.
You recognized what their last error offered and acted on it. That is how an opportunity becomes useful.
The comparison still favors another move. Examine what that alternative preserves.
A stronger alternative remains to be studied beside the move played.
The better choice was a different move. Set it on the board before drawing the lesson.
The passed pawn advances. Its distance to promotion shrinks, though the remaining obstacles still matter.
Reassess a passer after each advance. This one is closer to promotion now; examine the replies from here.
The strongest reply is a check. Any answer must first resolve that attack on the king.
Begin the comparison with the checking reply; it is the strongest answer here.
Precisely the move intended by the lesson. We may proceed.
Yes, you have supplied the lesson's answer at this position.
That agrees with the instruction here. On to the next part.
The answer is correct thus far. The puzzle still requires further play.
Well found. The puzzle has more to ask before it is finished.
That move is established. Now consider the next part of the puzzle.
Your recollection matches the opening line being studied.
Indeed, that move belongs to the repertoire passage at hand.
The stored line and your answer agree. Correctly recalled.
The strongest choice here. Let the merit of the move speak plainly: Best.
A precise answer to this position. It earns the Best mark.
This is sound, though a stronger move existed. Good deserves its own measure of respect.
Sound play is worth keeping, even while studying an improvement. This is Good, though a better move was available.
